human.title: Stuck? Talk to a person.
human.body: We’re in your time-zone, Mon–Sat. Pick whichever is easiest right now.

school.title: School
school.short: A government school we work with. Each school has classes, teachers and students.
school.long: A school is one of the 10 government schools the programme partners with in Leh and Kargil. Each school holds many classes (Grade 1, Grade 2…), has teachers, and runs sessions. Tap a school to see everything inside it.

class.title: Class (a grade)
class.short: One grade at one school — for example, Grade 3 at GPS Chuchot. It holds students and sessions.
class.long: A class is one grade at one school. Grade 3 at GPS Chuchot is one class; Grade 3 at GMS Khaltsi is a different class. Each class has a class teacher, students, and the subjects taught at that grade level.

subject.title: Subject
subject.short: What is being taught — English, Math, EVS, Hindi, Urdu, Science, etc.
subject.long: A subject is the topic area being taught — English, Mathematics, EVS, Hindi, Urdu, Science, and so on. Each subject is taught across a range of grades. Each subject has its own course outline per grade and term.

outline.title: Course outline
outline.short: The plan for one subject at one grade for one term — its learning outcomes and lessons.
outline.long: A course outline is the unit plan. For example: 'English G1 — Term 2: Decoding & blending'. It lists what students should learn, week by week, and how many sessions cover it. Sessions you teach link to this outline so you can see progress.

session.title: Session
session.short: One lesson in one classroom on one day. It has a date, time, teacher, topic and attendance.
session.long: A session is one teaching period — for example, the English lesson Tsering Dolma gave on 18 May 2026 to Grade 1 at GMS Khaltsi. It records the topic, the duration, who attended, and links to the lesson plan (outline) it came from.

teacher.title: Teacher
teacher.short: A government-school teacher in the programme. They teach sessions and grow through phases.
teacher.long: A teacher is a government-school teacher enrolled in the programme. Each teacher belongs to one school, teaches one subject, and is in one of the three RTT phases. They are paired with a mentor.

mentor.title: Mentor (Master Mentor)
mentor.short: An expert who guides up to 5 teachers — observes them, gives feedback, holds quarterly check-ins.
mentor.long: A mentor is a senior educator who works one-on-one with up to 5 teachers (called mentees). They observe lessons, hold quarterly check-ins, and write feedback. Each mentor specialises in a subject area.

mentee.title: Mentee
mentee.short: A teacher in a mentor's care — the same word for the teacher's side of the pairing.
mentee.long: A mentee is the teacher side of a mentor-teacher pairing. You will hear 'my mentor' (when the teacher speaks) and 'my mentees' (when the mentor speaks). It's the same relationship.

pairing.title: Mentor–mentee pairing
pairing.short: The link between one mentor and one teacher. It lasts one school year.
pairing.long: A pairing is the formal one-year link between a mentor and a teacher. Each pairing is reviewed every quarter (Q1–Q4). At year-end, pairings can rotate so teachers learn from different mentors.

student.title: Student / Learner
student.short: A child enrolled in a class. Their records are private — only school staff can see them.
student.long: A student is a child enrolled in a class. Records hold name, age, guardian and attendance. Because this is sensitive personal information, only school staff and programme leads can view it, and bulk exports are audited.

resource.title: Reading material / Resource
resource.short: A document teachers and mentors use — handbooks, lesson templates, policy notes, worksheets.
resource.long: A resource is any document tagged into the programme — NEP policy briefs, lesson handbooks, classroom routines, festival calendars. Each resource is tagged to one or more subjects so the right ones surface in the right place.

observation.title: Classroom observation
observation.short: A full cycle where a mentor watches a teacher teach and then they discuss it together.
observation.long: Classroom observation is a five-step cycle: (1) The teacher writes a short Pre-form explaining what they plan to do. (2) The mentor watches the lesson — live or via a video the teacher uploads. (3) The mentor watches the video again and writes notes at exact timestamps. (4) The mentor writes a Post-form with two strengths and one growth move. (5) Both sign off.

cycle.title: Observation cycle
cycle.short: One round of pre-form → lesson → post-form → sign-off, run between a teacher and a mentor.
cycle.long: A cycle is one complete round of observation. It has a unique code (like OBS-2026-001), a date, a topic, a kind (baseline, developmental or evaluative), and moves through five stages. A teacher can have several cycles in a year.

pre_form.title: Pre-form (Pre-observation)
pre_form.short: A short note the teacher writes BEFORE the lesson — what they plan, what they want help with.
pre_form.long: The Pre-form is the first step of every cycle. The teacher writes the lesson objective, the class context (how many students, any context), what they plan to try differently, and what they want the mentor to look out for. Keep it short — five lines is enough.

post_form.title: Post-form (Post-observation)
post_form.short: The mentor's feedback after watching the lesson — two strengths, one growth move, a small commitment.
post_form.long: The Post-form is written by the mentor after the lesson. It always has the same shape: two strengths to amplify, one specific growth move, ratings on four classroom domains, and one commitment for the next cycle. Short, kind, specific.

sign_off.title: Sign-off
sign_off.short: Both the teacher and mentor acknowledge the cycle is complete. It locks the record.
sign_off.long: Sign-off closes a cycle. Both the mentor and the teacher tap to acknowledge. Once signed, the record cannot be edited. If the teacher does not sign within 9 days, the programme admin is notified.

baseline.title: Baseline observation
baseline.short: The first observation in a teacher's journey — to understand where they're starting from.
baseline.long: A baseline cycle happens at the beginning. The mentor doesn't expect perfection — they're listening for the teacher's starting place so the rest of the year is targeted to what they need.

developmental.title: Developmental observation
developmental.short: A normal mid-term observation focused on growth — not graded.
developmental.long: Developmental cycles are about learning, not judging. The Post-form's only purpose is to help the teacher get better. Most cycles in a year are developmental.

evaluative.title: Evaluative observation
evaluative.short: A graded check, usually mid-year or year-end. Results count towards certification.
evaluative.long: Evaluative cycles happen at key milestones — mid-year and year-end. The Post-form contributes to certification at the end of Phase 3.

rubric.title: Rubric
rubric.short: A scoring sheet with four domains: climate, clarity, engagement, assessment. Each rated 1–5.
rubric.long: The rubric is the same across every cycle — four domains: Classroom climate, Instructional clarity, Engagement & participation, Assessment for learning. Each is scored 1 to 5. The mentor scores the same things every time so progress is comparable.

rtt.title: RTT — Refresher Teacher Training
rtt.short: Our three-phase programme that takes a teacher from refresher training to confident classroom leader.
rtt.long: RTT stands for Refresher Teacher Training. It is the three-phase journey every teacher goes through over two years: Phase 1 (Foundational), Phase 2 (Application), Phase 3 (Mastery & Certification).

phase.title: RTT phase
phase.short: The teacher's stage in the programme — Phase 1 (start), Phase 2 (apply), Phase 3 (mastery).
phase.long: Each teacher is in one of three RTT phases. They move from one to the next based on cycle outcomes and a mid-phase evaluation. Most teachers spend ~6 months in Phase 1, ~9 months in Phase 2, and ~9 months in Phase 3.

phase_1.title: Phase 1 — Foundational
phase_1.short: Onboarding and baseline. Teachers learn the basics: routines, classroom climate, lesson shape.
phase_1.long: Phase 1 is the foundation. The teacher is new to the programme. Focus: classroom climate, routines, lesson-planning basics, and starting to record video. Cycles are mostly baseline.

phase_2.title: Phase 2 — Application
phase_2.short: Putting it into practice. Teachers run live cycles with a mentor and join cohort sessions.
phase_2.long: Phase 2 is where the work begins. Teachers run regular developmental cycles, attend monthly cohort sessions, and complete their first major assessments. Most teachers spend the longest here.

phase_3.title: Phase 3 — Mastery
phase_3.short: The home stretch. Teachers do evaluative cycles and earn certification at the end.
phase_3.long: Phase 3 leads to certification. Teachers run evaluative cycles, may begin mentoring junior peers, and present a final portfolio.

district.title: District
district.short: Leh or Kargil — the two districts that make up the Union Territory of Ladakh.
district.long: We work in both of Ladakh's districts. Leh (the larger, lower-altitude district) and Kargil (further west). Each has its own zones, schools, and master mentor.

zone.title: Zone
zone.short: An administrative area inside a district — for example Khaltsi zone in Leh district.
zone.long: A zone is the level between district and school. Each district is divided into zones; each zone has 1–4 schools we work with. Mentors plan their travel route around zones.

term.title: Term
term.short: One third of the school year. Term 1 (Apr–Jul), Term 2 (Aug–Nov), Term 3 (Dec–Mar).
term.long: The Ladakh school year is split into three terms. Each term lasts about 12 weeks. Course outlines are written per term, so a subject can have three outlines in a year.

quarter.title: Quarter (Q1–Q4)
quarter.short: Mentor-mentee progress is reviewed four times a year — Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4.
quarter.long: Each pairing has four quarterly progress check-ins. Q1 = baseline + onboarding. Q2 = first developmental cycle. Q3 = mid-year evaluation. Q4 = endline & certification. The four bars on a mentee card show this progress.

feedback_form.title: Quarterly feedback form
feedback_form.short: Eight questions the mentor answers each quarter to log how the mentee is growing.
feedback_form.long: Every quarter, the mentor fills an 8-question form covering classroom routines, instructional clarity, growth area, and commitments for the next two weeks. Auto-saves every 5 seconds so you can finish it later.

commitment.title: Commitment
commitment.short: One concrete thing the mentee (or mentor) promises to do before the next cycle.
commitment.long: A commitment is the smallest possible behaviour change — for example, 'I will keep a 4-minute cool-down at the end of every lesson this week.' Mentor and mentee each leave one commitment per cycle. They're tracked openly so they don't get forgotten.

growth_move.title: Growth move
growth_move.short: The single most-important behaviour to change. Make it tiny and observable.
growth_move.long: The Post-form asks for ONE growth move. Not five. The discipline is: pick the one thing that, if it changed next week, would help the most. Keep it observable — something a colleague could see.

strength.title: Two strengths
strength.short: Two specific things the teacher already does well — name them so they keep doing them.
strength.long: The Post-form starts with strengths, not weaknesses. Name two things you saw the teacher do well — by name, specifically. This builds confidence and protects the relationship.

status_nominated.title: Nominated
status_nominated.short: A cycle has been created but the teacher hasn't filled the Pre-form yet.

status_pre_submitted.title: Pre-form submitted
status_pre_submitted.short: Teacher has filled the Pre-form. The lesson is ready to happen.

status_observed.title: Observed
status_observed.short: The lesson has happened (live or recorded). Mentor will now write the Post-form.

status_post_submitted.title: Post-form submitted
status_post_submitted.short: Mentor has written feedback. Waiting for teacher to acknowledge.

status_complete.title: Cycle complete
status_complete.short: Both have signed off. This cycle is closed and recorded.

status_planned.title: Planned
status_planned.short: This session is on the schedule but hasn't happened yet.

watermark.title: Watermark
watermark.short: Your name and the time, shown over the player while you watch. A reminder that classroom videos stay inside the programme.
watermark.long: While you watch a classroom video, your name and the current date and time are shown over the player, and every view is logged. The watermark is on the player, not in the video file itself, so it is a reminder rather than a lock: please do not share, download or re-record classroom videos.

hls.title: HLS streaming
hls.short: Streaming in short pieces that adjusts quality to your connection, so a video starts quickly and keeps playing on a weak signal.
hls.long: HLS sends a video in short pieces rather than as one large file, so playback starts before the whole video has arrived and a dropped connection only costs the piece in flight. Each video is streamed in up to three versions, 240p, 360p and 480p, and the player drops to 240p (about 250 kbps) when your network is weak and comes back up to 480p when it's strong. This is why videos play even in remote Ladakh schools on patchy 3G.

transcoding.title: Transcoding
transcoding.short: What happens to a video after upload — we re-make it as a 240p, 360p and 480p stream that plays in the browser.
transcoding.long: When a teacher uploads a video, our server converts it into three versions for streaming: 240p for a weak signal, 360p, and 480p, the sharpest (a video recorded smaller than that is never enlarged, so it gets only the versions that fit), plus a still frame for the video library. The player moves between them by itself as your signal changes. This takes a few minutes. While the system is transcoding, you'll see a 'Transcoding…' badge.

whatsapp_ingest.title: WhatsApp upload
whatsapp_ingest.short: Forward your lesson video to our WhatsApp number — it comes straight into the system.
whatsapp_ingest.long: Many of our teachers find it easier to send videos via WhatsApp than upload through the app. Send your video to the programme WhatsApp number with your cycle code as the caption, for example OBS-2026-009 (the code is shown on your cycle's page), and it will land on that cycle automatically. A long lesson can be attached as a document instead.

upload.title: Uploading from the browser
upload.short: You can also upload a lesson video straight from this app — best on stable wifi.
upload.long: Direct browser upload works on a phone or a computer. It resumes if your connection drops, but a large video needs a steady link, so use stable wifi where you can. On a slow or patchy network, sending the video by WhatsApp is easier. Either way, your videos appear on your Uploads page within a few minutes.

navigation.title: Finding your way around
navigation.short: On a phone, use the bottom tabs to switch between sections. On a computer, use the sidebar.
navigation.long: Every section you can use is one tap away: the bottom tabs on a phone, the sidebar on the left on a computer. Your settings, including the interface language, are under Settings in the sidebar on a computer, and behind your initial at the top of the screen on a phone. The ? button opens this help from anywhere.

password.title: Forgot your password?
password.short: Ask your programme admin to send you a sign-in link — it lets you in without the password.
password.long: If you cannot sign in, ask your programme admin to send a sign-in link to your email address. Open the link on the device you want to use, then set a new password from Settings. The section gate password (for Observation, Mentorship and Admin) is different: your programme admin shares that one separately.

section_gate.title: Section gate
section_gate.short: An extra password for sensitive areas — rotates every 30 days for safety.
section_gate.long: Some sections (Observation, Mentorship, Admin) require a second password after login — the section gate. It rotates every 30 days. Your programme admin shares the new code over a secure channel. Every attempt — correct or wrong — is logged.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.short: A record of every action — every login, view, edit, upload — kept for 7 years.
audit.long: The audit log keeps a permanent record of what happens in the system: who logged in, who viewed a video, who edited a record, who tried a wrong password. This is to protect everyone. The log cannot be edited or deleted, only read.

confidentiality.title: Confidentiality
confidentiality.short: Lesson videos, names of children, and mentor notes are private to the programme.
confidentiality.long: We treat every video, every child's record, and every mentor note as private. They are watermarked, never downloadable, and never to be shared outside the programme. The footer of every page reminds you of this.

role_super_admin.title: Super Admin
role_super_admin.short: Owns the system. Can do anything — including manage other admins.

role_programme_admin.title: Programme Admin
role_programme_admin.short: Day-to-day operations — teachers, schools, schedules, gates, reports.

role_mentor.title: Mentor
role_mentor.short: Carries up to 5 mentees. Observes, gives feedback, holds quarterly check-ins.

role_observer.title: Observer
role_observer.short: Visiting role. Can join an observation, but doesn't have ongoing mentees.

role_teacher.title: Teacher
role_teacher.short: The reason this all exists. Learns through phases, gets observed, grows.

attendance.title: Attendance
attendance.short: How many children turned up. Shown as 'present / total' — for example, 18 / 20.
attendance.long: Attendance is recorded by the teacher per session. We track it because attendance dips often explain learning dips. Stays-above-90% is the cohort target.

cohort.title: Cohort
cohort.short: A group of teachers who go through the programme together — they meet monthly online.
cohort.long: Your cohort is the group of teachers in your phase who came in around the same time. You attend cohort sessions together once a month, share lessons, and learn from each other.
